extracted.intended_audience: trademark office examiners, trademark searchers, IP attorneys, and national intellectual property offices implementing or using the Vienna Classification
extracted.subtask_description: Use and application of the WIPO Vienna Classification (Classification of Figurative Elements of Marks) for coding, publishing and searching figurative elements of trademarks. Includes rules for structure, numbering, notation, use in official documents, and governance of revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: facilitate anticipation searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Classification is essentially the practical one of facilitating trademark anticipation searches and obviating substantial reclassification work when documents are exchanged at the international level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Classification to make anticipation searching effective; classification should minimize reclassification when exchanging documents internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope determined by each country (non-binding on protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the requirements prescribed by the Agreement itself, the scope of the Classification is that attributed to it by each of the countries party to the Vienna Agreement; the Classification does not bind those countries in respect of the extent of the protection afforded to the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National offices may give the Classification the legal scope that best suits their needs and may apply it as principal or subsidiary system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical structure: categories, divisions, sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification constitutes a hierarchical system that proceeds from the general to the particular, dividing all figurative elements into categories, divisions and sections. Explanatory notes may concern a category, division or section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must understand the hierarchy when coding and searching; sections are the most specific level used for anticipation searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two kinds of sections: main and auxiliary
rubrics_metrics.description: The sections are of two kinds. In addition to main sections, there are auxiliary sections intended for figurative elements that are already covered by the main sections, but which it is considered useful to group according to a particular criterion for ease of anticipation searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections are for convenience in searching and are optional for national offices; they are associated with principal sections and often denoted with an 'A' prefix in the code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding system: three-number identification and auxiliary codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Every figurative element in a section is referred to by three numbers: the first (1–29) denotes the category; the second (1–19) the division; the third (1–30) the section. Auxiliary sections are indicated additionally (e.g., A 2.5.18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: representation of 'a little girl eating' is CFE 2.5.3, 18 (i.e., 2.5.3 and auxiliary section 18). Use the three-number code to uniquely identify figurative elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation/formatting of classification numbers (CFE and edition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbers of the category and division, and of the division and section should be separated by a point; numbers of two different sections by a comma; a dash indicates an uninterrupted range of sections; the edition should be indicated by an Arabic numeral in round brackets (e.g., CFE (7)). The Committee determined the abbreviation 'CFE' to precede classification numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: CFE 3.9.10,24,25 ; CFE 3.9.16-18 ; if only category and division: CFE 3.9. Always indicate edition as CFE (edition_number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple category/division coding: separate indications in numerical order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the numbers of several categories and divisions are necessary for the classification of one and the same registration, the classification for every category and division should be indicated separately, in numerical order; the various indications should be separated by a semicolon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CFE 1.1.2,10,25; 1.15.17; 2.9. If section numbers are not included: CFE 1.1; 1.15; 2.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to include classification numbers in official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent offices of countries party to the Vienna Agreement are obliged to include in the official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks the numbers of the categories, divisions and sections in which the figurative elements of those marks have been placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Documents and publications’ include trademark register entries, registration/renewal certificates and office journals or gazettes. The classification numbers should be preceded by 'Classification of Figurative Elements' or abbreviation CFE.

rubrics_metrics.name: National reservation on section numbers and auxiliary sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries party to the Vienna Agreement may declare that they reserve the right not to include the numbers of all or some of the sections in official documents and publications; auxiliary sections are in any event not mandatory and may be used at national discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices with few registrations may omit detailed section numbers; they may use Vienna as a subsidiary system while keeping national classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preconditions for effective searching: two interdependent operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For searching to be effective, two operations must be completed: (i) consistent and correct classification (coding) of the figurative elements in the search file, and (ii) correct definition of the sections in which prior marks have to be searched, taking account of the specific characteristics of coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both operations are interdependent and require skilled personnel to carry them out accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification should consider future needs of anticipation searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent and correct classification of the figurative elements of the marks that are to constitute the search file should take due account of the future needs of anticipation searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding, consider how codes will be used later for searches; avoid idiosyncratic or inconsistent coding that would impede future searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and required skills for classifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The two operations (classification and definition of search sections) must be entrusted to persons with proven skills in the trademark field. Those persons should, among other things, be able to assess the figurative elements of marks according to their distinguishing properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use trained examiners or specialists familiar with distinguishing properties of figurative elements; classification is not purely mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacant numbers reserved for future additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within divisions and sections, certain numbers have been left vacant in order to permit the introduction of new divisions or sections when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reassign reserved/empty numbers; they are intentionally kept for future revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples are illustrative only, not integral
rubrics_metrics.description: The examples of figurative elements relating to certain divisions are included for information purposes only, and are therefore not an integral part of the Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat examples as guidance; legal or coding decisions should rely on the Classification text and explanatory notes, not solely on pictured examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Vienna Classification as principal or subsidiary system
rubrics_metrics.description: The countries party to the Vienna Agreement may apply the Classification either as a principal or as a subsidiary system; they may continue to use their national classification at the same time as the Vienna Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices can run Vienna alongside national systems, e.g., transitional or permanent dual usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for auxiliary sections (prefix 'A')
rubrics_metrics.description: The numerical code of auxiliary sections is preceded by an 'A' in the Classification (e.g., A 26.3.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing an auxiliary section explicitly, include the 'A' to distinguish it from principal sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation when registration is entrusted to intergovernmental authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: If any country entrusts the registration of marks to an intergovernmental authority, it shall take all possible measures to ensure that that authority uses the Classification in accordance with Article 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must ensure third-party registries apply Vienna rules consistently with the Agreement's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision process and entry into force of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A Committee of Experts shall make amendments and additions to the Classification; every decision of the Committee concerning adoption of amendments shall be notified by the International Bureau and the amendments shall enter into force six months after dispatch of the notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must monitor Committee notifications and incorporate amendments after the six‑month entry-into-force period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of Experts composition and voting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee of Experts: each country of the Special Union represented; decisions require simple majority, but changes regarded by one-fifth as modifying basic structure or entailing substantial reclassification require three-fourths majority; each country member has one vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant structural changes require higher quorum/majority; proposals for amendments must be communicated two months before session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages and authentic texts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification has been established in English and French, both texts being equally authentic; the International Bureau may establish official texts in other languages designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the Classification legally or for official codification, refer to the authentic English or French texts; translations may be provided but English/French are authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for labelling classification in documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbers of the categories, divisions and sections appearing in official documents and publications relating to registrations should be preceded, for ease of comprehension, by the full name 'Classification of Figurative Elements' or by the abbreviation CFE, and the edition should be indicated (e.g., CFE (7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always prefix classification codes with CFE or the full name and indicate the edition number to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition lifecycle and replacement of previous editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editions of the Vienna Classification are published periodically; the seventh edition (published June 2012) enters into force on Jan 1, 2013 and replaces previous editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing codes, specify which edition is in force/used for classification; expect periodic consolidated editions that incorporate amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granularity: classification sufficiently detailed for anticipation searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification is sufficiently detailed for each section to contain only a relatively small number of figurative elements, thereby facilitating anticipation searches; it may be too detailed for offices with few registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full section granularity where volume warrants it; smaller offices may opt to omit some sections or use Vienna as subsidiary system.
